papers.title: Dissecting the genetic architecture for maize prolificacy by combining QTL mapping and genome-wide association study.
papers.abstract: Maize prolificacy (ears per plant) is a vital domestication trait in maize that profoundly determines grain yield potential. Deciphering its genetic regulatory network is essential for improving yield performance and expanding germplasm diversity. Here, we performed multi-environment phenotypic evaluation on two RIL populations and one association panel. Integrative QTL mapping and GWAS uncovered 13 QTLs and 8 QTNs associated with maize prolificacy. The stable locus qP9-2 harbored two tissue differentiation-associated genes (Zm00001eb395530, Zm00001eb395480), while the significant SNPs within
papers.journal: Molecular breeding : new strategies in plant improvement
papers.summary: This study dissects the genetic architecture of maize prolificacy (number of ears per plant) by combining QTL mapping in two recombinant inbred line populations with a genome-wide association study in an association panel, evaluated across multiple environments. The authors identify 13 QTLs and 8 quantitative trait nucleotides, including a stable locus (qP9-2) that harbors two genes linked to tissue differentiation. These findings provide candidate loci and genes for improving maize yield potential through breeding.

papers.title: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing reveals the 2'-O-methylation landscape and SNORD88B-guided FN1 modification in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To systematically map the internal 2'-O-methylation (Nm) landscape on messenger RNA (mRNA) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), characterize its distribution features and biological functions, and identify key C/D box small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs) that regulate Nm modification along with their target genes, thereby providing a molecular basis for elucidating post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms in HCC.
papers.summary: This study uses nanopore direct RNA sequencing to map the internal 2'-O-methylation (Nm) landscape on mRNA in hepatocellular carcinoma, characterizing its distribution and biological functions. It further identifies C/D box snoRNAs, particularly SNORD88B, that guide Nm modification of the FN1 gene, providing a molecular basis for post-transcriptional regulation in HCC.

papers.title: ABAQS: A comprehensive scoring method for assessing genome annotation quality.
papers.abstract: As genome resources continue to expand, estimating the accuracy and completeness of genome annotations (e.g., gene and protein models) becomes essential to ensure quality of downstream analyses and applications. It becomes critical in comparative genomic analysis to select genomes with comparable qualities of assembly and annotation. Without careful scrutiny, inconsistencies in annotation quality can undermine downstream studies.
papers.summary: ABAQS introduces a comprehensive scoring method for evaluating the quality of genome annotations, addressing the growing need to assess accuracy and completeness of gene and protein models as genome resources expand. The method helps researchers select genomes with comparable annotation quality for comparative genomic analyses, preventing inconsistencies from undermining downstream studies.

papers.title: hlafactor: a tool for multi-layer functional annotation of HLA variation.
papers.abstract: The human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system is the most polymorphic region of the human genome and a major determinant of immune function and disease susceptibility. Ideally, analyses of HLA variation would capture multiple layers of information, from classical alleles and amino-acid residues to higher-level functional properties such as tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups. However, while allele- and amino-acid-level data are now routinely available, the corresponding functional annotations remain scattered across publications and reference datasets, and no exis
papers.summary: hlafactor is a new software tool that consolidates multiple layers of HLA functional annotation—from classical alleles and amino-acid residues to higher-level properties like tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups—into a single resource. It addresses the current fragmentation of HLA functional data across publications and reference datasets, enabling integrated multi-layer analyses of this highly polymorphic immune region.

papers.title: DGIdb in 2026: an interoperable resource for the druggable genome.
papers.abstract: The Drug-Gene Interaction Database (DGIdb; https://dgidb.org) is an open-access aggregate knowledgebase that normalizes and centralizes drug-gene interaction and gene annotation data from diverse therapeutic and biomedical sources. Since its previous update, DGIdb has expanded its data content and added new tooling to better support programmatic access and local deployment. This release updates existing sources and incorporates three new sources of interaction data, including annotation data from the Molecular Oncology Almanac, the PRISM Repurposing Dataset, and the Broad Institute Drug Repurp
papers.summary: DGIdb 2026 is an updated open-access database that aggregates and normalizes drug-gene interaction data from many sources, now adding three new datasets including the Molecular Oncology Almanac, PRISM Repurposing, and Broad Institute drug repurposing data. The release also improves programmatic access and local deployment options, making it easier for researchers to integrate druggable-genome information into their own pipelines.

papers.title: Multi-centre implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome test for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Low-coverage whole-genome sequencing offers a scalable approach to homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) testing in ovarian cancer. This multi-centre study describes the real-world implementation of one such assay, SeqOne SomaHRD, across four European laboratories between 9 January 2023 and 1 October 2025. Tumours were classified as HRD-positive if they had a Genomic Instability score (GIS) of ≥0.50 (GIS-high) and/or a pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant. GIS was generated from two bioinformatically derived measures of genomic instability: Large-scale Genomic Alterations (LGA) and Loss of Parental
papers.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
papers.summary: This multi-centre study reports real-world implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome sequencing assay (SeqOne SomaHRD) for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer across four European laboratories. Tumours were classified HRD-positive based on a Genomic Instability score derived from large-scale genomic alterations and loss of heterozygosity, and/or pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants. The work demonstrates that low-coverage WGS-based HRD testing is scalable and feasible in routine clinical laboratory settings.

papers.title: DeGenRESOLVE: An offline GUI-based automated nanopore sequencing pipeline for viruses with custom rule-based indel and degeneracy resolution.
papers.abstract: Sequencing methods based on Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) have revolutionized the field of viral genomics. However, available analysis tools are often internet-dependent, have complex installation requirements, or lack graphical user interfaces (GUIs), limiting their use in laboratories with restricted internet access or limited bioinformatics expertise. Here we present DeGenRESOLVE, a pipeline designed for amplicon-based ONT resequencing where a reference genome is available. This pipeline does not perform de novo assembly but processes raw base-called ONT viral sequencing data offline i
papers.summary: DeGenRESOLVE is an offline, GUI-based pipeline for analyzing amplicon-based Oxford Nanopore sequencing data from viruses when a reference genome is available. It automates the workflow and includes custom rule-based resolution of indels and degenerate bases, addressing the need for tools that work without internet access or advanced bioinformatics skills. The tool is aimed at laboratories with limited connectivity or expertise.

papers.title: Auditing the adversarial robustness of genomic foundation models with SafeGenes.
papers.abstract: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) such as evolutionary scale modeling (ESM) are increasingly applied to variant effect prediction in clinical genomics, yet their adversarial robustness remains underexplored. We present SafeGenes, an evaluation framework combining input-space attacks, a discrete single-nucleotide variant (SNV)-reachable HotFlip attack, and a soft-prompt-triggered backdoor. Across cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia datasets, iterative attacks severely degrade discrimination: projected gradient descent (PGD) reduces the area under the curve (AUC) by more than 30 percentage points, and
papers.summary: SafeGenes is an evaluation framework that stress-tests genomic foundation models (like ESM) used for clinical variant effect prediction. It introduces input-space attacks, a discrete SNV-reachable HotFlip attack, and a soft-prompt backdoor, and shows that iterative attacks such as PGD can drop AUC by over 30 percentage points on cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia datasets. The work highlights that these models are far less robust to adversarial perturbations than their clinical use might assume.

papers.title: Computational and experimental strategies for functional validation of non-coding variants in pancreatic cancer.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterised by extensive genomic heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Although recurrent coding mutations in key driver genes have been well researched, large-scale sequencing studies have identified a broad array of non-coding variants which may contribute to tumorigenesis by interfering with gene regulatory mechanisms. However, understanding the functional significance of these variants remains a major challenge due to their abundance and the complexity of non-coding regulatory structures. This review outli
papers.summary: This review discusses computational and experimental strategies for determining which non-coding genetic variants contribute to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. It highlights the challenge posed by the abundance of non-coding variants and the complexity of gene regulatory mechanisms, and outlines approaches to prioritize and functionally validate them.

papers.title: MARiO: Predicting Cancer Variant Pathogenicity by Integrating In Silico Evaluation and Patient-Level Mutational Contexts.
papers.abstract: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) supports precision medicine in cancer care, but accurate assessment of missense variant pathogenicity, especially for variants without established consensus, remains challenging. Various computational tools have been developed for variant functional prediction, but most current tools rely solely on variant-level features and do not capture the clinical context of individual patients. To address this limitation, we developed MARiO (Missense Alteration Risk identifier in Oncology), a machine-learning model that integrates variant-level features and patient-l
papers.summary: MARiO is a machine-learning model that predicts the pathogenicity of missense cancer variants by combining variant-level in silico features with patient-level mutational context, addressing the limitation of existing tools that ignore clinical context. This integration aims to improve variant interpretation for comprehensive genomic profiling in precision oncology, particularly for variants lacking established consensus.

papers.title: Pooled multiplex amplicon massive parallel sequencing for high-throughput confirmation of whole-genome sequencing potentially pathogenic variants in patients with parkinsonism.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) identifies large numbers of genetic variants, although only a subset requires independent confirmation for clinical interpretation. Sanger sequencing remains the standard confirmation method but is impractical for large-scale variant verification. We developed and evaluated a strategy for variant confirmation based on multi-amplicon massively parallel sequencing of pooled DNA samples. WGS data were obtained from 86 individuals, including patients with parkinsonism and controls. Variants were selected using phenotype-driven filtering, ClinVar classification, and pa
papers.summary: The authors developed a pooled multiplex amplicon sequencing approach to confirm potentially pathogenic variants identified by whole-genome sequencing in patients with parkinsonism. By pooling DNA samples and using massively parallel sequencing of multiple amplicons, they provide a scalable alternative to Sanger sequencing for high-throughput variant validation. This method addresses the bottleneck of confirming large numbers of WGS variants in clinical and research settings.

papers.title: Detection of Maximal Exact Matches in Terabases of Genome Assemblies in Compressed Space and Sublinear Time.
papers.abstract: Detection of long exact matches between a pair of genomes has historically been a fundamental operation in genomics. Similarly, detection of long exact matches between all pairs of haplotypes in a large panel of genotyping array data or whole-genome sequencing variant calls is a fundamental operation in population genetics. Thanks to various recent pangenome efforts, for the first time, large panels of high-quality genome assemblies are being constructed. Therefore, we propose the intersection of these two approaches: detection of long exact matches between all pairs of assemblies in panels of
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper introduces a method for detecting maximal exact matches (MEMs) between all pairs of genome assemblies in large panels, operating directly on compressed data and in sublinear time. This enables scalable comparative genomics across terabase-scale pangenome collections, where pairwise MEM detection was previously computationally prohibitive.

papers.title: PHI: a Galaxy-based workflow for reproducible prophage-host interaction analysis and standardized viral-genomics reporting.
papers.abstract: Viruses that infect bacteria, known as bacteriophages or phages, are widespread in nature and play important roles in shaping microbial communities and ecosystem functions. Some phages can integrate into bacterial genomes as "prophages", where they may influence the biology of their host by carrying genes that affect metabolism, virulence, or environmental adaptation. Despite their importance, studying prophages and their interactions with bacterial hosts remains challenging because it typically requires combining many complex computational tools and can be resource-intensive.
papers.summary: PHI is a Galaxy-based workflow that integrates multiple computational tools into a single reproducible pipeline for identifying prophages in bacterial genomes and analyzing their interactions with hosts. It also standardizes viral-genomics reporting, making prophage analysis more accessible and consistent for researchers without extensive bioinformatics expertise.

papers.title: Accelerating discovery and integration from RNA to Protein with R2T2P.
papers.abstract: Integrating transcriptomics and proteomics data remains an unmet challenge in the post-genomics era, discouraging researchers from pursuing integrative approaches to molecular biology research. Leveraging the power of translation profiling, we present RNA to Translation to Protein (R2T2P), a computational platform integrating genome-guided transcriptome assembly with identification of translation and proteins, including a tailored differential analysis framework and support for multiple reference transcriptomes. We applied R2T2P to investigate a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular d
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: R2T2P is a computational platform that integrates transcriptomics and proteomics by combining genome-guided transcriptome assembly with translation and protein identification, plus a tailored differential analysis framework and support for multiple reference transcriptomes. The authors applied it to a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy, demonstrating its utility for integrative RNA-to-protein analysis.

papers.title: A multi-scale cell-type resolved map of trans -regulatory architecture in the aging human brain.
papers.abstract: Mapping genetic effects on distal genes and regulatory programs is essential for understanding how genetic variation influences complex diseases; yet trans -QTL discovery remains limited by weak effect sizes, extensive multiple testing and poor reproducibility. Here, we introduce TransMap , a generalizable computational framework that combines multi-scale trans -QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve the discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Beyond individual trans -eGenes, TransMap constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes that account
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors present TransMap, a computational framework that combines multi-scale trans-QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Applied to the aging human brain, it produces a cell-type-resolved map of trans-regulatory architecture and constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes that boost statistical power beyond individual trans-eGenes.

papers.title: A computational tool to predict how new coronavirus variants evade antibody defenses.
papers.abstract: The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants with mutations in the receptor-binding domain (RBD) poses a significant challenge to antibody-mediated immunity and ongoing vaccine effectiveness. In this work, we present RBD-Escape, a transparent and experimentally grounded computational framework for estimating how combinations of RBD mutations influence recognition by polyclonal neutralizing antibodies. The framework integrates deep mutational scanning (DMS) measurements from 33 monoclonal antibodies characterized across multiple independent studies and aggregates these data into a unified model of anti
papers.summary: RBD-Escape is a computational framework that predicts how combinations of mutations in the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain affect recognition by polyclonal neutralizing antibodies. It integrates deep mutational scanning data from 33 monoclonal antibodies across multiple studies into a unified model, aiming to forecast antibody evasion by new variants. The tool is designed to be transparent and experimentally grounded, supporting vaccine and therapeutic antibody development.

papers.title: A Batch-Processing Pipeline for RNA-seq Gene Abundance Estimation.
papers.abstract: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets provide valuable opportunities to investigate gene and transcript abundance across species, tissues, developmental stages, and experimental conditions. However, processing multiple datasets consistently remains challenging because sequencing runs may differ in library layout, read length, sequencing depth, metadata quality, and analytical settings. Existing RNA-seq workflows often depend on dedicated workflow managers, substantial computational infrastructure, or advanced bioinformatics expertise, which may limit their accessibility for routine analyses. We pr
papers.summary: The authors present a batch-processing pipeline for estimating gene abundance from RNA-seq data that handles heterogeneous datasets differing in library layout, read length, sequencing depth, and metadata quality. The pipeline is designed to be more accessible than existing workflow-manager-based approaches, reducing the need for advanced bioinformatics expertise or substantial computational infrastructure. It aims to enable consistent processing of multiple RNA-seq datasets for routine analyses.

papers.title: gcat, its_a_scam: modular tools for single cell data processing and per-cell quality control.
papers.abstract: The era of designing bioinformatic pipelines using open source tools is giving way to monolithic, and often proprietary, tools designed for end-to-end analysis, especially in the context of single cell data. While these tools are convenient for going from sequencing data to an almost complete data analysis "in a few clicks", they can strongly limit data use beyond standard analyses.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present gcat and its_a_scam, two modular open-source tools for single-cell data processing and per-cell quality control. They argue that the trend toward monolithic, often proprietary end-to-end pipelines limits flexibility and reuse, and that composable tools better support non-standard analyses.

papers.title: Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes.
papers.abstract: Plateau aquatic environments expose fishes to chronic cold, hypoxia, ultraviolet radiation and low productivity, providing natural systems for studying genomic features associated with environmental adaptation. Whether related fishes inhabiting similar cold-water plateau environments exhibit comparable or divergent genomic responses remains unclear. We compared two plateau cypriniform fishes, Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus, within a 12-species phylogenomic framework, integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, chromosome-scale synteny and
papers.summary: This study compares the genomes of two ecologically similar plateau fishes (Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus) within a 12-species phylogenomic framework, integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, and chromosome-scale synteny. The authors find contrasting candidate adaptive signatures between the two species despite their shared cold, hypoxic, high-UV plateau environments, suggesting that genomic responses to similar environmental pressures can diverge even among related fishes.

papers.title: Topological Data Analysis Identifies Copy Number Variation Subtypes of Bulls Associated with Fertility.
papers.abstract: Bull fertility is a polygenic trait of significant economic importance in dairy and beef cattle, controlled by multiple genetic variants, including copy number variations (CNVs). Conventional single-variant association analyses primarily evaluate marginal effects of individual loci, whereas CNV co-occurrence patterns require complementary approaches. This study applied topological data analysis (TDA) to identify groups of bulls based on genome-wide CNVR profiles and to assess their association with insemination success rate. A total of 88 bulls were included, and the presence/absence of 406 co
papers.summary: This study applied topological data analysis (TDA) to genome-wide copy number variation region (CNVR) profiles from 88 bulls, grouping animals by CNV co-occurrence patterns rather than single-locus effects. The resulting CNV-based subgroups were associated with differences in insemination success rate, suggesting that combined CNV patterns capture fertility-relevant structure missed by conventional marginal association tests. It demonstrates TDA as a complementary approach for polygenic trait analysis in livestock.

papers.title: Variant Classification of a Non-Protein Coding Gene: ACMG/AMP Specifications for RMRP from the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel.
papers.abstract: This study, conducted by the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel (ClinGen SCID-VCEP), aimed to adapt the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) framework for germline variant interpretation in RMRP . Unlike the protein-coding genes for which the framework was primarily developed, RMRP encodes a non-protein-coding RNA. Biallelic pathogenic variants in RMRP cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia, which can include severe combined immunodeficiency disease and other immune abnormalities.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This work adapts the ACMG/AMP germline variant interpretation framework specifically for RMRP, a non-protein-coding RNA gene whose biallelic pathogenic variants cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia and can include severe combined immunodeficiency. The ClinGen SCID Variant Curation Expert Panel provides gene-specific specifications to address the challenges of classifying variants in a non-coding gene, extending the standard framework beyond its protein-coding origins.

papers.title: Correction of the cytosine deamination artifacts in FFPE-based sequencing experiments.
papers.abstract: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues remain an essential resource for molecular studies, yet formalin-induced cytosine deamination introduces characteristic C > T/G > A artifacts that compromise the accuracy of next-generation sequencing analyses. Numerous computational methods and enzymatic DNA repair strategies have been proposed to reduce these artifacts, but no systematic comparison across tools and experimental conditions exists. Here, we evaluate the performance of seven computational approaches (SOBDetector, Ideafix, MicroSEC, FFPolish, DeepOmics FFPE/FFPE-PLUS, FFPErase) to
papers.summary: This paper systematically benchmarks seven computational tools designed to correct cytosine deamination artifacts (C>T/G>A substitutions) that arise in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue sequencing. The authors compare these methods across different tools and experimental conditions, addressing a gap where no prior systematic comparison existed. The work provides guidance on which correction approaches perform best for improving accuracy in FFPE-based next-generation sequencing analyses.

papers.title: quarTeT after 3 years: toolkit updates and community insights for telomere-to-telomere genome assembly.
papers.abstract: Since its initial release in 2023, quarTeT has become a widely used toolkit for telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly and characterization. Here, we present a major update that improves all four quarTeT modules, including optional contig filtering in AssemblyMapper, a refactored join algorithm in GapFiller, enhanced telomere detection in TeloExplorer (TE), and support for holocentric chromosomes in CentroMiner (CM). The main program has also been upgraded with user-configurable multithreading, broader version compatibility, and simplified deployment via Bioconda, Docker, and Singularity.
papers.summary: quarTeT, a toolkit for telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly, receives a major update improving all four of its modules: contig filtering in AssemblyMapper, a refactored join algorithm in GapFiller, enhanced telomere detection in TeloExplorer, and holocentric chromosome support in CentroMiner. The main program now offers configurable multithreading, broader version compatibility, and easier deployment via Bioconda, Docker, and Singularity. These updates make the widely used toolkit more robust and accessible for complete genome assembly projects.

papers.title: In silico analysis toward functional genomic profiling and bioprospecting Serratia rubidaea VITVS26 for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant potential.
papers.abstract: Proteases from bacteria and their secondary metabolites have bioactivity which can be utilized in therapeutical industries to overcome the negative effects of existing conventional medicines.
papers.summary: This study performed an in silico genomic analysis of the bacterium Serratia rubidaea VITVS26 to identify genes and pathways linked to anti-inflammatory and antioxidant potential, supporting its bioprospecting for therapeutic applications. The work highlights bacterial proteases and secondary metabolites as alternatives to conventional medicines with adverse effects.

papers.title: Identification and structural characterization of MMP1 and MMP9 as potential targets of curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a major subtype of lung cancer characterized by substantial molecular heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Curcumin and resveratrol are naturally occurring bioactive compounds with reported anticancer activities, but their potential molecular targets and mechanisms in LUAD remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses computational approaches to identify matrix metalloproteinases MMP1 and MMP9 as potential molecular targets of the natural compounds curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma, followed by structural characterization of the compound–protein interactions. The work suggests a mechanistic link between these dietary polyphenols and extracellular matrix remodeling pathways in LUAD, though the findings are based on in silico predictions rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Exploring the SWEET gene family and its role in root system architecture in Populus tomentosa.
papers.abstract: Sugars Will Eventually be Exported Transporters (SWEETs) facilitate sugar translocation and shape plant organ development, yet few studies have characterized their functions in root-related physiological processes in woody perennials.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the SWEET sugar transporter gene family in the woody perennial Populus tomentosa and investigates its role in root system architecture. It identifies family members and links their expression to root development processes in a tree species, extending SWEET research beyond model herbaceous plants.

papers.title: Genome-wide association study of growth-related traits in mandarin fish (Siniperca chuatsi): identification of cross-trait associated loci and candidate genes using single-trait and multivariate linear mixed models.
papers.abstract: Mandarin fish (S. chuatsi) is China's most economically important freshwater aquaculture species, yet selective breeding remains constrained by long generation intervals and limited genomic resources. We performed whole-genome resequencing of 98 Siniperca chuatsi individuals (minimum 10-fold coverage), retaining 1,310,398 quality-controlled bi-allelic SNPs across 24 chromosomes. Population structure analysis (principal component analysis, neighbor-joining, and ADMIXTURE) resolved four primary ancestral lineages that further separated into up to six finer-scale ancestry components, with evidenc
papers.summary: This study performed whole-genome resequencing of 98 mandarin fish to identify 1.3 million SNPs and used both single-trait and multivariate linear mixed models to find genetic loci associated with growth-related traits. They identified cross-trait associated loci and candidate genes, providing genomic resources to support selective breeding in this economically important aquaculture species.

papers.title: cgMLST typing reproducibility is maintained across diverse whole-genome sequencing workflows in a multi-country HERA2 surveillance pilot.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) has become indispensable in infectious disease surveillance, yet its implementation across laboratories remains heterogeneous. Six laboratories from four European countries participated in 2023 in a pilot ring trial as part of the HERA2 project, using a standardized panel of 25 bacterial isolates representing five public health-relevant species. The aim was to assess the comparability and reproducibility of laboratory-specific WGS workflows and to determine whether workflow-related variability affected cgMLST-based interpretations relevant for routine surveillance
papers.summary: This multi-country ring trial tested whether different laboratories' whole-genome sequencing workflows produce comparable cgMLST typing results for bacterial surveillance. Six labs in four European countries sequenced a standardized panel of 25 isolates across five public health-relevant species, and cgMLST-based interpretations remained reproducible despite workflow heterogeneity. The findings support the robustness of cgMLST typing for routine cross-laboratory surveillance.

papers.title: Computational functional annotation and structural modelling of hypothetical proteins in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia NCTC10958.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance represents a significant global health challenge, specifically concerning the escalation of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria. Stenotrophomonas maltophilia has emerged as a prevalent pathogen affecting immunocompromised patients in intensive care units. Its incidence has notably increased, particularly during the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic, complicated by resistance mechanisms such as enzymatic degradation and biofilm formation. Despite its clinical importance, the functional roles of many genomic regions remain obscure. This study aimed to characterize
papers.summary: This study computationally annotates and structurally models hypothetical proteins from the multidrug-resistant pathogen Stenotrophomonas maltophilia NCTC10958, assigning putative functions to previously uncharacterized genomic regions. The work highlights the potential of in silico pipelines to reveal proteins involved in resistance and biofilm formation, though experimental validation is lacking.

papers.title: Survey of viruses associated with the whitefly Bemisia tabaci in cucurbits in Georgia, United States.
papers.abstract: Whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) are major agricultural pests causing over $100 million in losses to vegetable production annually through the transmission of plant viruses. Characterizing the virome of B. tabaci is critical for understanding vectoring potential and identifying candidate viral biocontrol agents. In this study, B. tabaci were collected from cucurbit crops in Tifton, Georgia, across two consecutive years, 2023 and 2024. Total RNA was extracted and ribodepleted, then sequenced with 150 bp paired-end reads on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Bioinformatics analyses included quality-assessing
papers.summary: This study surveyed the virome of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) collected from cucurbit crops in Georgia over two consecutive years using RNA sequencing. The authors characterized the diversity of viruses associated with this major agricultural pest, which could inform understanding of virus transmission potential and identify candidate viral biocontrol agents. The work provides a baseline inventory of whitefly-associated viruses in this region.
